probe:mi.summary: MI does not pin the pose on I58bs — it is not a usable arbiter here. Raw Parzen-24 MI at 0.3 mm from P_R3, P_cand, P_v1 and 5 perturbed restarts each (3 mm / 5 deg) gives 18 distinct optima: no pair within 1 mm (block-corner mean), all-chain medoid radius 13.1 mm, per-start spread 10-14 mm. Every chain leaves its start by 4-10 mm (median 7.1) and 10-23 deg (median 17), MI rises x2.2, and 8/18 hit the -0.15 log-scale clamp (median ls -0.08). The same happens with the bias-flattened signal (fine.py's F_o/F_m): 18 singletons, median move 6.7 mm / 14 deg, MI x3.5, 6/18 at the clamp. The 0.15 mm level from the best 0.3 optimum drifts a further 4-7 mm (raw) / 3 mm (flat) instead of converging. The requested MI optimum (T_best = raw, 0.15 mm) sits 11.7 mm / 24.9 deg from P_R3 (centre shift along OCT z,y,x = +0.2, -3.1, +1.2 mm; log-scales -0.25,-0.24,-0.14 relative to P_R3) and 10.9 mm / 24.5 deg from P_v1; the flat optimum sits 13.3 mm / 33 deg from P_R3. A synthetic control (fixed image = MRI sampled at P_R3 + noise at the real MI level, truth = P_R3) returns to the truth within 0.04 mm / 0.07 deg from the same perturbations, so the drift is a property of the objective on these data, not of the optimiser or mask machinery. What MI does say consistently: the OCT-y translation should move negative (raw 15/18, flat 18/18 chains; translation-only optimum from P_R3 = -2.3 to -2.6 mm in y, x inconsistent -2.2..+2.1, z ~0), the same direction as P_cand (y -1.3) and the y+ face is the worst outline face at P_R3 (3.4 mm). Everything else (rotation, scale) is a runaway: MI maximises by shrinking the block and rotating it so that the OCT specimen mask lands inside a smaller, more homogeneous MRI region; the outline rejects both MI optima (MRI-tissue boundary inside the OCT block drops from 61 % at P_R3 to 39 % raw / 43 % flat, the deep-end face worsens 1.95 -> 2.65 mm), the fine NCC drops (0.120 -> 0.064 at 0.3 mm, 0.085 -> 0.071 at 0.15 mm) and the polarity guard weakens (flat optimum: mixed). At 0.3 mm the raw MI landscape behaves like a soft two-class WM/GM-plus-cerebellar-rind overlap, i.e. it shares the structural stage's rotation ambiguity rather than resolving it.
probe:mi.recipe: Script work/probe_xr/mi/p6_mi.py (CPU, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty, 4 threads, <= 2 processes, <= 1.8 GB each). Data: work/v11/I58bs_s40 (destriped oct150, texture mask, MRI 0.08 mm); levels built with octreg.fine.Level exactly as fine_stage does (0.3 mm: OCT pooled x2, MRI pooled x4 = 0.32 mm; 0.15 mm: OCT native, MRI pooled x2; MRI box = full volume as in the run). Specimen mask per chain/level = Level.spec_mask(T at level start) = erode_ball(MRI tissue, 1.3 mm) via T & OCT texture mask & eroded validity; each evaluation intersects with MRI tissue sampled through the evaluated pose (fine.MI32 / qc_fine convention). Objective: Parzen-window MI, 24 bins, Gaussian bandwidth 1 bin truncated at +-2 bins, raw OCT vs raw MRI (signal 'raw') or fine.py's 3 mm bias-flattened z-scored F_o/F_m (signal 'flat'); bin edges = 0.5-99.5 percentiles fixed at the chain start; hard 32-bin MI (verified identical to fine.MI32: 0.07473 at P_R3/0.3 mm, 0.06100 at 0.15 mm) and Studholme NMI reported alongside. Parametrisation: delta about identity in OCT world about c_o, T = T_start @ P(rotvec deg, t mm, isotropic log-scale clipped to +-0.15 with a penalty). Optimiser: scipy Nelder-Mead (adaptive, xatol 0.02, fatol 2e-6, maxfev 1500), rigid (6, simplex 2 deg / 1 mm) then similarity (7, 1 deg / 0.5 mm / 0.03). Chains at 0.3 mm: 3 starts x (unperturbed + 5 restarts: 5 deg about a random axis and 3 mm in a random direction, same 5 perturbations for every start); clustering = single linkage at 1 mm block-corner mean distance (8 block corners from oct150 shape/affine); centre = best-MI member of the largest cluster (all singletons -> overall best). 0.15 mm level from that centre + 2 restarts (1 mm / 2 deg), every 2nd m_spec voxel (~1.1 M points), maxfev 500, xatol 0.01. Evaluate: at P_R3, P_cand, P_v1 and the four MI optima, both levels, m_spec at the pose, common edges fixed at P_R3; also MI with the P_R3 mask (fixed point set) and without the tissue intersection; polarity_guard; sign-corrected flattened NCC via fine.make_refiner(..., 'ncc') = 1 - evaluate_T. Boundary via scripts/qc_fine.py unchanged (run dirs run_best / run_best_flat with T_oct2mri = optimum, T_oct2mri_prefine = T_oct2mri_structural = P_R3, T_oct2mri_fine_candidate = P_cand, result.json copied; run_v1 with T = P_v1, --skip-landscape) so boundary numbers for all poses use the same texture mask. Extras: 1-D profiles at P_R3 (rot +-25 deg, trans +-6 mm, log-scale +-0.15; both signals), translation-only and translation+scale optima with rotation fixed (both signals, 3 starts), synthetic control (fixed image = MRI sampled through P_R3 at the m_spec points + Gaussian noise 3 sd (MI 0.049, the real level) and 1 sd (MI 0.31); restarts 1-3 of the same perturbations).

probe:mi.caveats: (1) Mask dependence: within a chain the specimen mask is fixed at the chain start (fine.py convention) and the tissue intersection stays at N/N0 >= 0.9 (median 0.96), so the intersection bias alone cannot explain a x2-3 MI gain; but between chains and levels m_spec is re-derived at the current pose and grows with the shrink (7.2 cm3 at P_R3 -> 9.7 cm3 at the raw optimum), which rewards the shrink at the next level. The shrink is a degeneracy of this specimen: the OCT texture mask (17.6 cm3) is larger than the MRI tissue (13.3 cm3), so scaling the block down puts the whole mask inside eroded MRI tissue while the sampled MRI region becomes more homogeneous (H_mri 2.98 -> 2.89); the +-0.15 clamp is the only thing that stops it. The outline rejects these poses. (2) Raw MI at 0.3 mm is dominated by the gross bright/dark contrast (cerebellar folia vs brainstem in the MRI, surface vs deep in the OCT): it acts like a soft two-class overlap, which is exactly the structural stage's ambiguous objective; the bias-flattened signal (3 mm) removes the trend but not the ambiguity (MI values 0.01-0.045, near the estimator noise; its optima are as scattered). (3) Interpolation: 0.3 mm level uses MRI pooled x4 (0.32 mm) and OCT pooled x2 with trilinear sampling; the 0.15 mm level used every 2nd m_spec voxel (the log's 'cm3' label for 0.15 chains is therefore half the true mask volume). The Parzen estimator bias (B-1)^2/2N is ~1e-3 nats at 0.3 mm and negligible at 0.15 mm; MI is not comparable across levels or across masks of different N, only within one table row. (4) Optimiser: Nelder-Mead with a 3 mm / 5 deg perturbation set and maxfev 1500 (0.3) / 500 (0.15); the chains stopped on fatol, not on maxfev, so they are converged local optima, and the synthetic control shows the same machinery recovers a true pose to < 0.05 mm; a larger budget would only run further away. (5) The 'best cluster centre' for the 0.15 mm level is ill-defined (all singletons); I used the best-MI chain as the code specifies, and the finer level did not pull it back. (6) The translation-only optima with rotation fixed depend on the start pose and the signal (y consistently -2 to -3 mm from P_R3, x anywhere from -2 to +2), so even the translation should not be taken from MI alone. (7) MI32 QC landscape at P_R3 is a monotone slope on all axes at the range ends, so the earlier 'MI says >= 2 mm and >= 5 deg off' reading is not a local optimum statement either. (8) P5's pose (work/probe_xr/surf/T_best.npy) did not exist at the end (surf/ holds only landscape.json, optimise*.json and PNGs), so it was not evaluated; rerun `python work/probe_xr/mi/p6_mi.py evaluate --extra ...` from run_stage3.sh once it appears (60 s). (9) The polarity guard sign was -1 at every pose except the flat optimum (mixed, 0.47-0.52 negative), so NCC values were computed with sign -1 throughout. (10) The bounding MRI box is the whole MRI volume (as in the pipeline run), so the P_v1 chains sample the same MRI data as P_R3's; no crop differences. (11) All runs were CPU-only with 4 threads and never more than 2 concurrent processes; nothing outside work/probe_xr/mi and /tmp was written.

probe:surface.summary: P5 verdict: a surface-distance objective does NOT pin the OCT->MRI pose on I58bs. The loss is smooth but nearly flat in rotation (shoulder/min contrast 1-6 % over +-10 deg vs 10-32 % over +-4 mm), its minima lie 4 mm / 22-44 deg away from every intensity pose, and restarts fall into several basins whose losses differ by < 3 %: Huber+affine 21 starts -> basins at 12.1 mm (27.5 deg) and 9.5 mm (21.7 deg) block-corner distance from P_R3 plus two P_cand-only basins (max pairwise 17.5 mm; best cluster 8/21 within 0.67 mm); trimmed-80 % -> 5 basins, 7/21 within 1.27 mm, max pairwise 23.6 mm; rigid-only -> a flat valley 26-44 deg from P_R3, 5/21 within 1.47 mm, per-start spread 3.8-11.7 mm. Mechanism: the OCT texture mask (17.6 cm3) is 32 % larger than the cleaned MRI tissue (13.5 cm3; raw 13.3), i.e. the two 'surfaces' are ~1.4 mm apart radially, so every similarity/affine optimum shrinks the block 22-32 % along one OCT axis (log-scale delta -0.25 to -0.33) and rotates ~28 deg to make the outlines coincide; at those poses MI32 halves (0.075 -> 0.02-0.04 at 0.3 mm; qc_fine 0.0502 -> 0.0252) and the sign-corrected NCC drops from 0.12 to ~0.04 or negative (polarity guard reports mixed sign). The FOV-cut-face artefact in the MRI EDT is not the cause (an EDT without the cut faces reproduces the same basin). Adding lam*(1-sNCC) with lam in {0.5,1,2} does not move the optimum (still the 28 deg basin, MI 0.03) - lam 0.5 merely breaks the tie between the two basins and tightens 10/10 runs to 0.95 mm; lam 20-50 (the weight needed for the intensity term to matter, since 1-NCC varies by ~0.05 while Loss_sym varies by ~1) returns the poses to 4-7 mm / 4-16 deg from P_R3 (near P_cand, MI32 0.055-0.086) but the restarts scatter over 4-12 mm. T_best (task rule: tightest cluster, then MI, then boundary median) = P_R3_r4@lam0.5: 4.03 mm / 27.9 deg / block corners 12.1 mm from P_R3, 6.08 mm / 35.9 deg / 14.9 mm from P_v1; qc_fine rim median fwd 1.19 / rev 0.82 mm (P_R3: 1.96 / 1.26) but MI32 0.0252 vs 0.0502 and MI argmax at the +-5 deg / -2 mm range ends on 7/9 axes. The QC figure shows the outline matched to ~0.5 mm in the 6-14 mm planes, still 2-3 mm off at 19-23 mm depth, and the internal fibre-bundle pattern rotated relative to the OCT with the MRI visibly compressed - outline agreement bought with an anatomically wrong pose. Recommendation: do not use surface distance as an objective (any DOF) on this pair; keep it as the qc_fine measure only, or at most as a rigid-only regulariser weighted <= 0.05 relative to (1-sNCC), after the mask mismatch is fixed.
probe:surface.recipe:
EXACT LOSS AS BUILT (work/probe_xr/surf/surf_probe.py, CPU, 4 threads, ~75 s per 500-iteration run):
1. OCT surface points: qc_fine.py definition copied verbatim - B = (oct150_mask & ~erosion(oct150_mask)) & erosion_2(oct150 > 0) & (>= 3 vox from box faces) = 205,695 usable rim voxels; face class from -grad(gaussian(mask, 2)); the deep-end class z+ (42,517) is EXCLUDED -> 163,178 points in OCT world (oct150_affine, 0.15 mm).
2. MRI target: cleaned tissue = fill_holes(closing(mri_tissue, ball 2)) with components >= 1 mm3 (qc_fine clean_mask) on the full 0.08 mm grid (343x489x495; 13.5 cm3); boundary = tissue & ~erosion (662,488 voxels, includes the MRI FOV cut faces exactly as qc_fine); d_m = EDT(~boundary, 0.08 mm) as a torch float32 [1,D,H,W] (332 MB); sampled with octreg.common.sample_at_world (trilinear grid_sample) at T*p -> differentiable in T. Points whose T*p lies within 1 mm (12.5 vox) of an MRI FOV face are dropped (detached mask, recomputed every iteration).
3. Reverse term: MRI boundary voxels >= 1 mm from the FOV faces (618,015) mapped through inv(T) (torch.linalg.inv, differentiable); keep those >= 3 vox inside the OCT box and on valid OCT (erosion_2(oct150>0) at the rounded index) -> sample d_o = EDT(~B_rim, 0.15 mm) where B_rim = B minus the z+ class.
4. Robust means: Huber delta = 1 mm, rho = 0.5 d^2 (d <= 1), d - 0.5 (d > 1), mean over the USED points; trimmed = mean of the lowest 80 % (threshold via kthvalue, detached). Loss_fwd = mean rho(d_fwd); Loss_rev = mean rho(d_rev); Loss_sym = Loss_fwd + Loss_rev (weights 1:1). Optimised: sym_huber (main) and sym_trim (variant). Alternative 'fixedN' normalisation implemented but not run.
5. Optimiser: fine.py parametrisation reused unchanged - SurfRefiner subclasses fine._DeltaRefiner/refine.Refiner: delta D about identity, T = T_start @ D, D = compose(r, t, ls, sh, c_o) about the block centre c_o = [15.88, -20.01, 14.54]; Adam + cosine annealing (Refiner.refine), lr_rot 0.01, lr_t 0.15, lr_ls 0.005, lr_sh 0.005, ls/sh clamps 0.15 PER STEP, reg 0.5; schedule rigid 200 -> similarity 100 -> affine 200 iterations (variant: rigid-only 300). Restarts: params_from_matrix(T_start, c_o) then rotvec + 5 deg about a random axis, t + 3 mm in a random direction, log-scale + U(-0.03, 0.03) per axis (6 per pose; 4 in the combined runs).
6. Combined: Loss = Loss_sym_huber + lam * (1 - sNCC), sNCC = fine.FineRefiner masked NCC of the 3 mm-flattened intensities at the 0.3 mm level (fine.Level, MRI pooled to 0.32 mm), sign -1 (I58 guard), m_spec = eroded MRI tissue via T_start & OCT mask & validity (fixed per run as in fine.py), MRI tissue sampled through T as a detached weight; lam in {0, 0.5, 1, 2} (task) and {20, 50} (added because 1 - sNCC only varies by ~0.05 across the landscape while Loss_sym varies by ~1 mm).
7. Landscape: T @ P with P = fine.perturb_matrix(kind, OCT array axis, amount, c_o) (identical to qc_fine's perturb): translations -4..+4 mm step 1, rotations -10..+10 deg step 2.5 about c_o, log-scale -0.08..+0.08 step 0.02; 9 samples per axis; reported: grid and parabolic argmin, unimodality (single interior local minimum), contrast = (mean of the two end values - min) / min.
8. probe:surface.caveats:
1. QC figure at T_best (looked at qc_best/qc_fine.png): the cyan MRI outline now hugs the white OCT outline to ~0.5 mm on the top and right rims of the 5.8, 10.2 and 14.4 mm planes (where P_R3's orange dashed outline sat 1-3 mm inside at the top-left and outside at the bottom), but (a) at 18.8 and 23.1 mm depth the MRI outline is still 2-3 mm off (upper-left overhang at 18.8 mm, whole outline shifted up-right at 23.1 mm) - the loss ignores the deep-end class and the fit degrades there; (b) the internal anatomy no longer corresponds: in the checkerboards at 10.2 and 14.4 mm the OCT fibre bundles run at a visibly different angle from the MRI's (the 28 deg rotation), the bright folia-like MRI tissue in the lower-left of the 5.8 / 10.2 mm planes has no OCT counterpart, and the MRI appears compressed along one direction (23 % shrink); the MRI FOV edge cuts diagonally through the upper-right. Outline agreement was bought with an anatomically wrong pose.
2. The two 'surfaces' are not the same surface: OCT texture mask 17.6 cm3 vs cleaned MRI tissue 13.5 cm3 (raw threshold mask 13.3; the MRI was cropped to the OCT block and truncates the specimen: 17-24 % of the rim points map within 1 mm of the MRI FOV faces). Median rim distance stays >= 1.05 mm at every optimum. Until the OCT specimen mask and the MRI tissue mask are shown to delineate the same boundary (e.g. compare both against the raw images at a few rim locations), a surface term measures mask bias, not pose.
3. Chained clamps: refine_delta resets T0 at each step, so the 0.15 'relative clamp' applied per step (similarity then affine) and the cumulative log-scale change reached -0.35; a single overall clamp of 0.15 would still allow the 0.25 shrink needed to absorb the volume mismatch, so this does not change the conclusion but the reported ls deltas exceed 0.15.
4. Mean-over-used-points normalisation (the task's definition) has a coverage exploit: the lowest-loss trimmed solutions moved MRI boundary points out of the OCT box (n_rev 410k -> 277k). Huber runs did not show it (n_fwd rose, n_rev roughly constant). The fixedN alternative is implemented but not run.
5. The cleaned MRI boundary includes the FOV cut faces (scipy erosion treats the array border as background), as in qc_fine; OCT points 1-3 mm inside the FOV are pulled toward these fake faces. A cut-face-free EDT (cache/d_m_use.npy) was run for one affine start only (same basin A) before that job was stopped to stay within the 2-process limit; the rigid + cut-face-free combination was not run.
6. MI32 / NCC numbers in my JSONs use fine.Level (MRI pooled to 0.32 / 0.16 mm, m_spec = eroded raw tissue via T & OCT mask & validity, bin edges at the pose) and are only comparable within my tables; qc_fine's raw-0.08 mm MI32 is lower (P_R3 0.0502 vs my 0.0610 at 0.15 mm). The NCC term used the fixed sign -1; at most surface optima the polarity guard returns 0 (mixed), so the sign-corrected NCC there is not well defined.
7. Restart perturbations add 5 deg to the rotation vector (not an exact 5 deg composition) and 3 mm to the block-centre translation; actual perturbation moves are recorded per run. Six restarts per start pose is a small sample for a landscape with >= 4 basins.
8. The best-pose pooling labelled the rigid and affine Huber runs under one variant key ('huber/mean/all', 8/42); this did not affect the selection (lam 0.5 won with 10/10) but the ranking line in the log is misleading for that entry. T_best is affine (det 0.57 relative... i.e. 23 % shrink along OCT x) and should not be used as a registration result; it is written only because the task asked for the cluster-selected pose and its QC.
9. The lam >= 20 runs (my addition) show that when the intensity term dominates, the surface term neither tightens the restarts (4-12 mm spread) nor moves them away from the P_R3/P_cand neighbourhood; they also expose a second high-MI pose 26 deg from both P_R3 and P_v1 (MI32 0.0856, sNCC 0.150), i.e. the intensity landscape itself has comparable optima - the pose question is not settled by any combination tested here.
10. Compute: all CPU, 4 threads per process, max 2 processes, RAM <= 2.2 GB per process; nothing outside work/probe_xr/surf and /tmp was written. The FOV-free affine job (D) was killed by PID after one run.
